method: First independent review of the supplied bytes: atomscan slow scans, cleave facts including decoded text, Rizin/Capstone x86/x64 control-flow analysis, dnfile/dncil resolved IL, PE/ELF header and resource inspection. No sample was executed. Scores and family labels were leads, not behavioral evidence.

external_context.provided_feed_pages: MalwareBazaar and tria.ge pages could not be read through the web tool; no sandbox claim was promoted to an observed effect.
external_context.hash_recovery: forager recovered the exact a5dadf... file through MalwareBazaar hash fallback. SHA256 and size 2654208 match the supplied truncated specimen; artifacts and .forage.json are retained in scratch.
external_context.stock_control: Original upstream XMRig 6.24.0 static x64 release fetched with forager. Its executable SHA256 0c748b9e8bc6b5b4fe989df67655f3301d28ef81617b9cbe8e0f6a19d4f9b657 agrees with the accompanying SHA256SUMS. It is an external benign comparator, not a reconstruction of the submitted file.

samples.identification: Modified XMRig miner with shell-command concealment and redundant persistence
samples.marker_line: Modified XMRig: hides cron and resists removal; add stealth traits
evidence: Entry 0x407017 supplies main 0x4027ee to libc startup. main recognizes --libbase-run and a libbase.sh invocation, routing to 0x43148b. That routine calls the user-profile installer 0x430f92 and system-profile installer 0x431189. readlink(/proc/self/exe), self-copy and profile-writing paths establish installation mechanics beyond string presence.

The recurring worker at 0x42dd08 calls 0x42be62 then sleeps and loops; 0x430a18 likewise loops through 0x42dd1a. These routines construct cron relaunch entries for files under /var/tmp and HOME, install a systemd service/timer, and update shell profiles. Root/non-root branches query geteuid through syscall stub 0x53d6a3.

0x42c378/0x42c394 construct service and timer bodies; 0x42c3ba/0x42c41b pass their paths into installation helpers. Later command construction reloads systemd, enables and starts the timer. OnCalendar=*:0/1 and repeated @reboot/minute cron templates implement redundant relaunch capability.

0x42d5b5 and 0x42f46d load the crontab function body, append it into profile content through 0x42a322, and rewrite profile files through 0x44ca2a. The shell code excludes selected entries from crontab -l, restores them after editing, and reinstalls them when crontab --remove is requested. It also supplies a kill() wrapper that drops SIGKILL options and a top() wrapper that deletes selected output rows.

Cleanup routine 0x4303c4 loads the pkill/rm command at VA 0x550c3b, checks geteuid, calls it through 0x534182, and repeats. That helper constructs /bin/sh execution. The command kills competitor-named processes and removes HOME shell history plus the two /var/tmp files. Package-manager log erasure is not established.

RandomX initialization, mining/hash code, Stratum parsing and SupportXMR failover pool configuration establish XMRig-derived mining capability. Mining alone is dual use. Concealed crontab state, resistance to removal, shell-command interception and unwanted reactivation explain the malicious collection context and outweigh an ordinary miner explanation.

Cleave facts contain 237 XOR-decoding candidates and mechanical URL decodings, including printf-format strings. These are retained as decoded-content metadata; plausible-looking decoded text is not treated as executed obfuscation. The concrete concealment scripts are present in plaintext and have code references.

samples.marker_line: NjRAT Horror: keylogs, remote commands and MBR wipe; clarify camera
evidence: Unsigned managed PE; entry token 0x0600007a is j.A.main (RVA 0x8a54), which calls j.OK.ko (0x6e5c). ko starts RC and kl.WRK threads without the optional install/anti-analysis switches.

Configuration initializes H=DarkAlotaibi-48808.portmap.host, P=48808 and VR=<- NjRAT 0.7d Horror Edition ->. connect (RVA 0x30b0) supplies these fields to TcpClient.Connect; RC (0x7408) receives length-framed bytes and passes complete messages through _Lambda__1 to Ind (0x3790). This is a configured command channel, not an incidental networking API.

kl.WRK (0x8910) polls keys 0..255, maps them to characters, records foreground-window context and appends Logs, periodically persisting through STV. Ind command kl Base64-encodes those Logs and calls Send. Other Ind paths CopyFromScreen, JPEG-encode captured pixels and send CAP responses.

Ind accepts plugin payload bytes; Plugin (0x7338) calls Assembly.Load, searches loaded types and creates the selected instance. Command branches also launch programs and issue destructive commands. Base64 handling in DEB/ENB and gzip support are real serialization/loading mechanics, not evidence that the entire sample is encrypted.

MBRSlayer.Start (0x7b20) initializes a 512-byte embedded boot image, calls CreateFile on PhysicalDrive0 with GENERIC_ALL and OPEN_EXISTING, and supplies that buffer and count 512 to WriteFile. The routine is reached by the FuckMBR/FuckMBRNR command branches; one also requests forced reboot. Success requires adequate privilege and was not tested.

INS implements Defender realtime disabling, service stop/delete, UAC disabling and scheduler persistence, but their configuration switches are Disabled. Idr/IsF/Isu/USB_SP/Anti_CH are False. The VM-rejection text is a disabled message option, not evidence of an actual VM probe. Existing findings correctly describe command/message references or retained capabilities; none is removed merely because a startup branch is disabled.

Cam (0x2fc0) enumerates driver descriptions and returns device availability. No supplied routine captures webcam frames. The corrected suite preserves keylog, screen, camera-enumeration and TCP coverage without asserting video acquisition. Remote tasking, covert collection and reachable raw-disk destruction establish MALICIOUS independently of family identity.

samples.identification: StormAttack / Shtormec-style damaged persistence and DLL-injection loader
samples.marker_line: StormAttack loader: Active Setup, DLL injection and self-delete
evidence: Unsigned x86 PE; entry 0x402674 calls dispatcher 0x401cb0. Mode DWORD at file 0x4120 is 3. The selected branch 0x401f75..0x401f8f calls Active Setup installer 0x401900 and self-delete helper 0x401390.

Installer 0x401900 constructs a GUID-named HKLM Active Setup Installed Components entry, sets REG_EXPAND_SZ StubPath at 0x401a4b, reads its own image with CRT file APIs, patches and writes a self-copy at 0x401b26, and attempts CreateProcessA at 0x401b7e. The code implements durable login activation and self-relaunch.

Alternative mode code at 0x401260 constructs a System32 DLL path, opens LanmanServer/Parameters, deletes ServiceDLL at 0x401320 and writes its replacement at 0x40133e. The current initial mode does not select this branch; the finding describes retained replacement/injection code.

Injector 0x401150 launches a calc/notepad/Internet Explorer target, allocates remote memory, writes the DLL path, resolves Kernel32!LoadLibraryA through GetModuleHandleA/GetProcAddress, and uses that resolved export and remote buffer in CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d. This is DLL injection, not inferred process hollowing.

Self-delete 0x401390 obtains its own module path, converts it to a short path, reads COMSPEC, appends /c del plus the current image path, and launches the cleanup through CreateProcessA at 0x4014b8 and ResumeThread at 0x4014d9.

All 40960 raw bytes of .rsrc are zero, so the resource-directory/DLL extraction path cannot supply its original resource payload. Bound IAT fields are partly overwritten by GUID text, and copy patch offsets reflect another layout. Installation and execution success are not established. The 32020-byte overlay contains string/GUID-like data, no MZ image and no demonstrated activation path.

Retained code-section bytes 0x1000..0x289a have SHA256 98f975dd8b8d9f2e6da736754ef8f87a112e7f7e5f4d104b3f5e385e525c70c4, consistent with existing StormAttack loader fixtures. Those fixtures were context, not proof: all relevant paths were independently disassembled here. There is no supported WannaCry encryption or ransom claim. Unsolicited service replacement, injection and self-delete justify MALICIOUS despite damage. No YAML behavior changes were needed.

corrections: package-log-removal previously matched /var/tmp/apt.log and /var/tmp/yum.log. The sample also targets processes named apt.log/yum.log in that same cleanup command; neither location nor suffix establishes genuine package-manager logs. Retain the exact original matcher as notable fs/delete/file/command::apt-yum-named-temp-file-removal. Require actual /var/log/apt/history.log, /var/log/apt/term.log or /var/log/yum.log in the package-log objective, and prevent another semicolon-delimited command from supplying the path. Keep its hostile history-plus-package-log composite available for genuine log wiping.

Relocate system-helper-service-path with its exact matcher and elf/go scope from masquerade/identity/service to os/service/config, at notable criticality. A chosen helper-service filename alone cannot establish a fake service. Update the exact existing staged-C2 consumer; its required observation set remains unchanged. New OS/service/config ancestor consumers are Windows PE-only and cannot gain this Linux ELF/Go observation. No generic filesystem ancestor consumer gained an unrelated finding in the sample rescans.

Rename the .NET multi-source suite to dotnet-keylog-screen-camera-enum-tcp-suite and describe camera enumeration. capGetDriverDescriptionA does not capture video. Keep every matching condition, criticality and exclusion unchanged. Remove unsupported camera capture, installation, application-layer-protocol and conditional-execution mappings; retain keylogging, screenshot and raw TCP mappings.

Add generalizable crontab concealment/removal-resistance and SIGKILL-option-discarding shell-wrapper observations. The cron and systemd persistence composites require the concealment evidence plus their own activation surfaces. No payload filename, service basename, address, exact file size or hash gates the new hostile detections.
consumer_and_fixture_audit: Exact package-log-removal/native-history-and-package-log-wipe references are confined to elf.yaml. No other available sample under the named samples root contains /var/tmp/apt.log (rg -a -l -F audit). Existing dockerfile-log-hygiene fixture uses /var/log/apt and remains outside the ELF-only rule scope; the real-package-log positive control retains the intended attack coverage.

No rule references the old .NET suite ID; the only non-definition reference was a historical Helios binder review. That review identifies a decoded RAT with the same SHA256 as this batch, corroborating packaging context after independent IL review. Historical scan IDs were not rewritten.

Audited exact and ancestor directory selectors for the helper relocation, log correction, new wrapper observations and neutral file-deletion observation. The relevant new service-config consumers are PE-scoped; broader filesystem consumers either have incompatible scopes or retain independent requirements. Actual before/after report diffs show only the documented changes.

coverage: genuine package-log deletion plus history wiping

remaining_limitations: The outer ELF has load segments and a section-header table extending beyond EOF. Its embedded ELF at file 0x1634b8 is also truncated: it declares a 1615886-byte load image but only 1198920 bytes remain. Its entry 0xc1f400 is absent. UPX markers and header structure survive, but upx -d refuses it. The embedded file was independently scanned and its facts saved; no missing payload behavior or successful execution is invented.

The ordinary outer scan reports one file and does not automatically carve this truncated child. The separate child scan records packing/structure observations and ML probability 0.8981959 with level -1; its final program and intent cannot be established. Its UPX rejection diagnostic is engine-emitted and does not prove that the bytes were never packed.

anti-analysis/malformed/elf-header is an engine-emitted legacy ID. The malformed structure is real; it does not prove deliberate anti-analysis. There is no YAML rule to relocate or suppress, and no shadow or sample exception was added.

No original deployment authorization, victim telemetry, runtime success or attacker identity is available. The deception, intrusive control and destructive code tip the judgments. The source of the Linux truncation and StormAttack resource erasure is unknown.

Atomscan warns that the installed v18 model specification is older than the v19 feature producer. All three final parent scans agree with MALICIOUS; the initially uncalibrated Linux result is resolved by supported new behavior coverage, not by restoring the inaccurate log/service claims.
detection_losses: No supported attack coverage was lost: shell history deletion remains suspicious, temporary-file deletion remains notable, helper-path recognition is preserved under its neutral home, and the .NET suite is a matcher-preserving rename. The Linux package-log hostile composite correctly stops firing on temporary-file names; the real package-log/history positive still fires. StormAttack findings are unchanged. All final parent classifier results are hostile at calibrated level 25.
